experts.activation_rule: softcap(gate, g) * sigmoid(gate) * softcap(up, u), softcap(x, c) = c * tanh(x / c), in float32

router_rule.weights: unbiased scores of the selected / (sum + 1e-20) * route_scale

nvfp4_g16.global_scale: amax * 6 * 448 / denominator; w = e2m1 * e4m3 * global / (6 * 448)
nvfp4_g16.code_dtype: fp4_e2m1, two per byte, low nibble = even element

q8_rule.matrices: the six attention projections (q, k, v, r, o, gate) of every layer and the output head
q8_rule.embedding: not copied: one bf16 row per token is read from resident.safetensors

features.layout: x = [rmsnorm(emb) * emb_norm.weight, h_prev, h_lag]; h_lag absent for applications a < lag
features.emb: embed_norm(embedding row) (the embed_tokens output of transformers PR 51050); the router normalises it again with its own weight
features.h: the MoE block input of the application; h_prev at application a for the previous token (zero at position 0), h_lag at application a - lag for this token
features.output: z = lin.weight @ x + lin.bias + mlp.2.weight @ gelu(mlp.0.weight @ x + mlp.0.bias) + mlp.2.bias; the top m of z name the experts of application a

training.code: jobs/babel/ink_router.py + jobs/babel/babel_ink_best.sh (8 x 1024 tokens per step, ink_r_main's data and schedule)
training.objective: KL(pi || softmax(z)), pi = 0.5 uniform over the released top-8 + 0.5 its renormalised weights

derived.made_by: moved-store python/derive/inkling2_loop_xtok.py --from routers/xtok_s41_h512.safetensors --targets 0-5 --bits 8 (8-bit, the first six target applications; the engine itself does not derive this kind)
moved-store python/derive/inkling2_loop_xtok.py --from routers/xtok_s47_h512.safetensors --targets 0-5 --bits 8 (8-bit, the first six target applications; the engine itself does not derive this kind)

derived.for: memory-limited iPhones (the phone-small profile) only; tokens differ from the 8-bit set
derived.made_by: ms_derive resident DIR --bits 4 --from-calibrated FILE (the head and the six attention projections of each layer from a calibrated 4-bit export, every other tensor as the plain 4-bit set)
derived.quality: with the NVFP4 late layers, top choice equal to the exact 8-bit engine on 0.934 / 0.961 of prose / agent-text positions in exact mode (plain 4-bit: 0.923 / 0.940); fast at a 1.7 GB cache 0.911 / 0.943 (measured on the Mac)

pending: vision.safetensors (636,563,560 B) left out (recommendation: not uploaded); --with-vision lists it as an optional extra
unknown: vision.safetensors: listed in sha256.txt but not on the Mac

generated.by: moved-store release tools, from the manifest of 2026-11-21 plus the new parts

exact.definition: Generated tokens never depend on the cache, the routers or timing: the model's own router picks 8 experts per layer and the engine waits for every one.

fast.definition: The model's own router still picks. A picked expert that is not in memory is waited for if its routing weight is over 0.1 or its read is already in flight; otherwise it is left out (no substitute, no renormalisation). Router names are on.

mac.cache_rule: locked; size chosen from free memory at start (ceiling = physical memory - 5.5 GB - the process's other memory); shrinks 1 GB per check under memory pressure and grows back
mac.optional_note: the background cross-token source (source 41); the release's draft head (dmeng --draft head|both, command-line tool only), which also needs resident.safetensors (its output layer is folded from the bf16 unembedding)
mac.bytes_rule: sum of the listed parts' bytes; moved-store.json is fetched first and is not listed

phone.when: iOS with at least 5.0 GB available at open
phone.cache_rule: locked slab sized at open: available - in-memory weights - router - 0.3 GB - 0.9 GB margin, clamped to 0.6-8 GB
phone.bytes_rule: sum of the listed parts' bytes; moved-store.json is fetched first and is not listed

phone-small.when: iOS with less than 5.0 GB available at open (the 6 GB class)
phone-small.precision_detail: 4-bit affine, groups of 64, calibrated (resident_q4); experts' layers 20-23 as NVFP4
phone-small.cache_rule: locked slab sized at open: available - in-memory weights - router - 0.3 GB - 0.9 GB margin, clamped to 0.6-8 GB
phone-small.status: top choice equal to the exact 8-bit engine, prose / agent text: exact 0.934 / 0.961, fast at a 1.7 GB cache 0.911 / 0.943 (Mac); a device run is still to do

experts.note: layers 20-23 re-quantised from the release's MXFP8 to NVFP4 (least-squares block scales); the release's files stay as they are for the other profiles

notes.routers: linear_k2 names experts 2 steps early (one linear layer: about a fifth of the MLP's router bytes per token); its engine file is derived/router.linear_k2.q8...bin; mlp_k2_h512 stays available (--routers or routers_id)
notes.cross_token: source 47 names the next token's experts for its first six steps (engine targets 0-5), with priority reads
notes.prompt_path: batched span prefill, prefix cache with disk checkpoints, idle-time prefill of the next turn, saved hot set
notes.drafts: --drafts 1 is experimental (lookup and tool-call skeleton drafts, greedy requests only); the release's draft head through the command-line tool only (the mac profile's optional parts)

cross_token_routers.role_in_engine: dmeng --xtok FILE (source 47) and --xtok-bg FILE (source 41, a background second source)

features.output: the top m of z = lin(x) + mlp.2(gelu(mlp.0(x))) name token t+1's experts at application a

training.note: trained by imitation of the next token's released routing; data and token count are not recorded in the exported file

notes: cross_token_routers: not in `routers` because the engine's manifest reader expects every entry there to name all 48 steps (targets == steps); the engine reads them through dmeng --xtok

layout.rule: engine-ready files are in derived/ under the engine's own names (<id>.<engine_format>.<first 12 hex of the source part's sha256>.bin); the engine looks for them in DIR/derived/ as well as DIR/.dmeng/ and derives what is missing into DIR/.dmeng/
layout.profile_rule: the engine picks the profile from the device; --profile NAME overrides it, --mode exact|fast overrides the profile's mode
